_comment: F-16A CAP (Combat Air Patrol) mission-profile inputs for Mission Analysis (subplan 07). Single JSON, not split by fidelity level: unlike Geometry's L1/L2 (genuinely different input schemas), the CAP segment data (altitudes, Mach numbers, given range/time, payload drop, and the scalar high-lift/ground-roll constants below) is IDENTICAL across MissionL1/L2/L3 -- only the per-segment COMPUTATION METHOD differs by fidelity (fixed-fraction/Table-2.2 Breguet at L1, single-point Breguet with real aero/prop objects at L2, sub-segmented Breguet + energy-height climb at L3). F16MissionL1/L2/L3's constructors are all expected to read this same profile.
_source: docs/subplans/07_mission_analysis.md, section 'F-16 CAP Mission Profile' (user-approved 2026-07-24, including its own explicit verification caveat); underlying data attributed there to temp_Casey/inputs/Mission_Profile.xlsx, sheet 'CAP'.
_verification_status: VERIFIED against the live Mission_Profile.xlsx CAP sheet (2026-07-24, coordinator pass, via Python openpyxl since no MATLAB execution tool was available -- functionally equivalent to the readtable/readcell check the earlier scribe/io passes couldn't run). Every segment_names/alt_ft/mach_end/dist_nm_given/time_min_given/drop_lb value below was diffed against the live cell values and matches exactly (dist_nm_given values are the raw ft figures -- 1154462.8/303806/1458268.8 -- converted at 6080 ft/nm, matching the sheet's raw 'Range (ft)' row). No corrections were needed. examples/F16A/Mission_Profile.xlsx has now been created (binary-copied via shell, not Write) from temp_Casey/inputs/Mission_Profile.xlsx. One new field was added below (dry_or_wet) that the live sheet carries but this JSON previously omitted; see its note.
_note_segment_names: CAP has 10 segments vs. Brandt's Miss-tab 14 -- Accel and Egress are the only Brandt legs genuinely absent from CAP (Brandt's other 4 extra segments -- Patrol/Patrol2/Patrol3/Climb2 -- are 0-duration bookkeeping waypoints, not distinct legs; see subplan's dated 2026-07-24 user clarification, 'CAP mission profile vs. Brandt's 14-segment Miss-tab profile' section). 'Cruise'/'Cruise2' naming (outbound/return) mirrors Brandt's own two-cruise-leg naming convention (VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:mission.segment_names) for consistency with the established dispatch-loop pattern (legacy MissionAnalysisLevel1's segment_<name> string match, digit-stripped before comparison). The subplan's table itself labels these rows 'Cruise (outbound)'/'Cruise (return)' -- the literal CAP-sheet column header text was NOT confirmed (see _verification_status) and may need to change once MissionProfileImporter reads the real sheet.
_note_alt_ft: Altitude AT END of each segment (matches the f16a_geometry.json:mission.altitude_ft convention). Source: subplan 07 CAP table, column 'Alt (ft)'.
_note_mach_end: Mach number AT END of each segment. Source: subplan 07 CAP table, column 'Mach'. UPDATED 2026-07-24 (user correction to the live source spreadsheet, temp_Casey/inputs/Mission_Profile.xlsx CAP sheet): Takeoff 0.87->0.282 (now matches Brandt's Miss-tab liftoff Mach exactly, resolving the oddity flagged the same day in VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md's 'Finding B'), Loiter 0.30->0.31, Landing 0->0.3. Re-verified directly against the live sheet after the user's edit -- all three new values confirmed present in the live 'Mach number' row.
_note_dist_nm_given: Given range per segment [nmi]; null = not a range-given segment (time-given, or n/a). Source: subplan 07 CAP table's ft figures (Cruise=1,154,463 ft, Dash=303,806 ft, Cruise2=1,458,269 ft) converted to nm at 6080 ft/nm (the same conversion factor VnV/BrandtF16A/BrandtMission.m uses, e.g. 'd_nm = d_ft/6080') -- matches the subplan's own '~189/~50/~239 nm' parenthetical approximations exactly. Property name 'dist_nm_given' matches the Tier-3 input list in subplan 07's 'Input vs. derived properties' section. NOT independently verified against the live sheet (see _verification_status).
_note_time_min_given: Given duration per segment [min]; null = not a time-given segment. Source: subplan 07 CAP table's 'Range / Time' column (Combat=2 min, Loiter=20 min) -- both values exactly match Brandt's Miss-tab Combat/Loiter times (VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:mission.time_min_given), a reassuring cross-check even without live-Excel access to the CAP sheet itself.
_note_drop_lb: Payload jettisoned during the segment [lbf]. Source: subplan 07 CAP table's 'Payload drop' column -- Combat=4,400 lbf exactly matches Brandt's Miss-tab Combat drop_payload_lb (VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:mission.drop_payload_lb) and the live CAP sheet's own 'Payload, drop (lbf)' row (confirmed 2026-07-24). The subplan's separately-stated 'Fixed payload throughout: 5,100 lbf' also matches the live sheet's 'Payload, fixed (lbf)' row (5100 for all 10 segments) exactly, and equals f16a_geometry.json:weight.perm_payload_lb (700) + weight.exp_payload_lb (4400) = 5,100.
_note_dry_or_wet: Afterburner state per segment, from the live CAP sheet's 'Dry or Wet' row (added 2026-07-24 -- this field existed in the live sheet and in the legacy MissionAnalysisModel.get_mission_data extraction but was not carried into the earlier draft of this JSON). Determines which TSFC method F16MissionL2/L3 call per segment: prop.get_TSFC(state) (mil power) for 'Dry' segments, prop.compute_TSFC_AB(state) for 'Wet' segments (Dash, Combat). At L1 this is unused (L1 does not call prop at all, per subplan 07's Design Notes) but is carried here since it's a genuine CAP-profile input, not a derived quantity.
_note_turns_unused: The live CAP sheet also has a 'Turns' row (value=2 for Combat only, blank elsewhere) not represented in this JSON. Not needed by the Roskam Eq. 2.12-based Combat equation documented in subplan 07 (which uses a directly-assumed L/D, not a load-factor/turn-count derivation), but flagged here as available source data in case a future refinement adopts Mattingly's alternative turn-based combat form (subplan 07's 'Mattingly-form alternative' section, Eq. 3.25) which does use load factor n.
_source_scalars: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json:mission (CLmax_TO, CLmax_land, mu_rolling, liftoff_factor, warmup_fuel_per_engine_lb) -- these are genuine F-16 aircraft/configuration constants (high-lift CLmax, ground-roll friction coefficient, liftoff-speed margin factor, engine warmup fuel), not values specific to Brandt's Miss-tab mission profile, so reusing the already-cited Brandt Main-tab figures for the CAP profile (same physical aircraft) is traceable and does NOT hardcode a Brandt calibration/sizing OUTPUT into the F-16 subclass (cf. PLAN.md's Cfe/e_osw rule) -- these are aircraft input spec values. NOT independently confirmed that Mission_Profile.xlsx's own CAP sheet carries identical copies of these constants (see _verification_status) -- if the live CAP sheet has its own values for these, a follow-up pass must reconcile which one F16MissionL1/L2/L3 should actually read.
